rows.settlement_scope: Standard full-game only; verify local rules and market exceptions
rows.model_status: Experimental independent forecast; no validated betting edge

inputs.label: Opponent shots allowed / game
inputs.detail: Recency-weighted; the same figure the game-line model uses

inputs.label: His results vs. our forecasts
inputs.detail: 541 actual vs. 567.2 forecast shots in earlier games; shrunk toward 1

steps.label: Opponent shots allowed vs. long-run league average
His results vs. our past forecasts

build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many shots the opponent allows compared with the league. Then adjusted for how he has done against our own forecasts: 541 shots against 567.2 forecast in his earlier games, shrunk toward no adjustment. The model then turns this average into the chance of each count.

blend.label: Production rate
blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

blend.label: Ice time
blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

trend.label: SOG
trend.note: Faded games count less. A game’s weight halves every 110 of his games for production and every 14 of his games for ice time.

missing: The starting goalie (team defense blends its goalies)

versus.note: History only, not a model input. In our backtests, results against one opponent did not predict the next meeting beyond a player’s overall form.

player_context.note: Newer appearances carry more weight. Ice time has a 14-appearance half-life; production per minute has a 110-appearance half-life. The offseason does not age player history. Expected shots scale with the opponent’s shots allowed, and scoring with its goals allowed, relative to the league. A player who has consistently beaten (or missed) our earlier forecasts gets a shrunk adjustment toward that record. Observed averages below are unweighted. Participation and current role remain unconfirmed.

key_drivers: Projected ice time 16.7 minutes; separately shrunk production rate
uncertainties: Line and power-play assignment not verified
invalidation_conditions: New goalie, lineup or injury information
rows.goalie_assumption: Projected, not confirmed. Opposing goalie, Winnipeg Jets: likely Stuart Skinner 66% (sv 0.896), Clay Stevenson 34%.
rows.lineup_assumption: Participation required for action; current role and active lineup unconfirmed

sensitivity.assumption: Production/opportunity means ±10%; not a confidence interval

assessment.reason: The model edge is moderate and holds across the sensitivity range. Settlement rules are published, and no Cirelli-specific adverse report is supplied.
assessment.model_case: Projected mean of 1.65 shots is above 1.5. The under depends on a median of one shot over 16.7 projected minutes. Because the mean exceeds the line, the case is distribution-driven rather than volume-driven.
assessment.price_case: At +125 the break-even sits below the model's fair price near -107. The low sensitivity bound still clears break-even narrowly. Two other books support only a modest gap, so the case is not extreme.
assessment.context_case: A Tampa winger is day-to-day with a fresh update. The effect on Cirelli's linemates and minutes could cut either way, and no Cirelli-specific reporting is supplied.

qualitative_review.countercase: Tampa absences could push Cirelli into more offensive or power-play minutes. With a mean above the line, a small usage increase makes two shots more likely than the model allows.

reviewed_candidate.model_status: Experimental independent forecast; no validated betting edge

inputs.label: Opponent goals allowed / game
inputs.detail: Recency-weighted; the same figure the game-line model uses

inputs.label: His results vs. our forecasts
inputs.detail: 141 actual vs. 128.7 forecast points in earlier games; shrunk toward 1

steps.label: Opponent goals allowed vs. long-run league average
His results vs. our past forecasts

build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many goals the opponent allows compared with the league. Then adjusted for how he has done against our own forecasts: 141 points against 128.7 forecast in his earlier games, shrunk toward no adjustment. The model then turns this average into the chance of each count.

blend.label: Production rate
blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

blend.label: Ice time
blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

trend.label: points
trend.note: Faded games count less. A game’s weight halves every 110 of his games for production and every 14 of his games for ice time.

missing: The starting goalie (team defense blends its goalies)

versus.note: History only, not a model input. In our backtests, results against one opponent did not predict the next meeting beyond a player’s overall form.

player_context.note: Newer appearances carry more weight. Ice time has a 14-appearance half-life; production per minute has a 110-appearance half-life. The offseason does not age player history. Expected shots scale with the opponent’s shots allowed, and scoring with its goals allowed, relative to the league. A player who has consistently beaten (or missed) our earlier forecasts gets a shrunk adjustment toward that record. Observed averages below are unweighted. Participation and current role remain unconfirmed.

key_drivers: Projected ice time 16.3 minutes; separately shrunk production rate
uncertainties: Line and power-play assignment not verified
invalidation_conditions: New goalie, lineup or injury information
reviewed_candidate.goalie_assumption: Projected, not confirmed. Opposing goalie, San Jose Sharks: likely Yaroslav Askarov 56% (sv 0.892), Alex Nedeljkovic 44%.
reviewed_candidate.lineup_assumption: Participation required for action; current role and active lineup unconfirmed

sensitivity.assumption: Production/opportunity means ±10%; not a confidence interval

reviewed_candidate.review: Price or forecast changed · research needs recheck

review_context.validation: Experimental; no established executable betting edge

assessment.reason: At +126, the break-even probability sits below the model's estimate, even at the low end of sensitivity. The opponent is missing two forwards. Settlement rules are assumed rather than checked, which is a routine verification and not a material blocker.
assessment.model_case: A projected mean of about 0.70 points on 16.3 minutes against a 0.5 line is a reasonable opportunity case. The weakness is that line and power-play assignment are unverified, and history may not reflect Rossi's current Vancouver role.
assessment.price_case: Main line 0.5 at +126; break-even is about +126 against model fair odds near even money. The low-end sensitivity case stays above +126 implied, but the margin is narrow. Consensus comes from only two other books.
assessment.context_case: The listed Sharks absences may modestly weaken San Jose, but no source addresses Rossi's deployment. His own status is unverified, and absence from the table does not establish health.

qualitative_review.countercase: If Rossi is deployed off the top power-play unit or in a checking role, his point rate could fall below the history-based estimate. The narrow cushion over break-even would then disappear. Goalie uncertainty between Askarov and Nedeljkovic adds variance either way.
